newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Lightning shuts down Taiwan commuter railway.
newsitem.headline: Lightning shuts down Taiwan commuter railway.

text.p: Lightning caused an emergency shutdown of Taipei's French-built commuter railway on Wednesday, transit officials said.
"Mucha line's operations have been temporarily shut down because of the lightning. We are evacuating passengers. Nobody is hurt," a spokeswoman at the city government said.
She said 11 commuter trains were operating when the lightning struck, adding that it was the second time the line's operations had been halted by lightning.
The Mucha line, the first of Taipei's six planned commuter lines, was built by French contractor Matra Transport.
The elevated 11-km (6.8-mile) Mucha line opened on March 28, 1996, five years behind schedule after a spate of fires, burst tyres on transit cars, and derailments during test runs.
The US$18 billion Taipei mass transit system is said to be the world's most expensive at US$220 million per km ($354 million per mile).
Matra suspended its Taiwan operations in May 1996 over a row with the Taipei city government.
